plan: [ It's a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding (bid = value) is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies and avoids the risk of negative profit from overbidding (paying a second price above my value). Underbidding risks losing when I would have profitably won. With no prior rounds to learn from and uniform values, I will bid my exact value to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is a second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value: overbidding can cause negative profit if it flips a loss into a win at a price above value; underbidding can forgo positive-profit wins. With no prior rounds to infer rivals’ behavior and values uniform 0–49, bid exactly 22 to win whenever both rivals’ bids are below 22, paying the second-highest bid and guaranteeing nonnegative profit. No shading needed in this one-shot round. ]

[ One-shot, private-values, second-price auction. With independent values and payment equal to the second-highest bid, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value, yielding negative profit; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive profit (paying at most the second-highest bid ≤ your value). No history to exploit this round. Therefore, bid exactly your value to maximize expected profit. ]
